etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle French dogmatique and its etymon, Late Latin dogmaticus, from Hellenistic Ancient Greek δογματικός (dogmatikós, “didactic”), from δόγμα (dógma, “dogma”).
senses: (philosophy, medicine) Adhering only to principles which are true a priori, rather than truths based on evidence or deduction.
One of an ancient sect of physicians who went by general principles; opposed to the empiric.
